artifact.canonical_name: OPEN Alliance TC9 Automotive Ethernet Channel & Components specifications

sources.title: TC9 – Automotive Ethernet Channel & Components
sources.role: Official OPEN Alliance committee page used for cabling/channel requirements, test methodology scope and current focus.

claims.text: TC9 defines electrical requirements and test procedures for automotive Ethernet cabling channels and components, including cables, connectors and assemblies aligned with IEEE 802.3 link-segment requirements.
The committee states that its work covers automotive Ethernet speed grades on electrical media and develops generic measurement/test procedures for link-segment and component qualification.
The pinned page states current work includes 1000BASE-T1 over coaxial media and 25GBASE-T1, while the roadmap lists 10BASE-T1S channel/component requirements v1.1 from June 2025.

limitations.text: This page verifies channel/component specification activity and versions, not electrical performance of any particular production harness or connector implementation.

targets.target: Verify the official scope/status and architecture-significant statements on open-alliance-channel-components; distinguish directly checkable facts from organization/project claims.
targets.finding: The official page establishes physical-channel/component responsibilities and test methodology spanning multiple Automotive Ethernet media/speeds.

editorial.why_now_note: Physical link/channel specifications are an often-hidden but essential constraint on the move to Ethernet-centric zonal/backbone architectures.
editorial.rationale: Strong supporting candidate for the physical-network layer, especially to prevent the survey from treating Ethernet as a purely logical/software transition.
